title: Native Uint64 Bitwise V1
objective: Implement generic source-transparent typed uint64 bitwise and shift operators in IR, dynamic fallback, native C lowering, explain/inspect output, and differential property tests with defined shift semantics
scope_notes: The lane expanded from native-compiler to compiler-runtime after the frontend revealed that Sage mode normalized CPython xor to exponentiation even under the existing explicit native-bitwise marker. The only frontend change preserves `^` and `^=` under that marker and leaves ordinary Sage exponentiation unchanged.

handoff.summary: Implemented canonical typed uint64 &, |, ^, <<, and >> operations across exact, binary64, and source-transparent prime IR plus portable JavaScript, isolated C, word, tagged, and prime-source backends. Augmented scalar and UInt64Buffer lowering preserves Python target-before-RHS evaluation order, uses explicit 0..63 shift guards, logical right shift, and modulo-2^64 left shift. Sage-mode native-bitwise source now preserves xor and uses checked full-word dynamic helpers for mixed exact Number/BigInt values rather than JavaScript 32-bit operators. Prime-source Node returns preserve the full unsigned range as BigInt, exposed JavaScript fallbacks validate the public ABI, and adversarial tests cover 2^40, 2^63, 2^64-1, invalid operands, shift 64, mixed representations, dynamic fallback, native C, and portable JavaScript. IR v22, cache fingerprinting, explain metadata, host/policy benchmark metadata, compiler documentation, and Node test-manifest registration are included.
risks: The broad compiler tier failed outside this claim: compiler/algebra.py timed out and compiler/matrix.py hit an existing sparse-random runtime error under Node 26.7.0.
The broad integration tier passed 371/380 tests but failed eight matrix/polynomial runtime tests outside this claim; focused native-kernel, FFI, build, architecture, and strict checks pass.

CPython's annotation-only uint64 fallback retains Python int left-shift behavior; full-word wrapping and 0..63 guards are the documented typed-IR/native/portable-JavaScript contract, so a CPython oracle that reaches overflow or an out-of-range shift must make that boundary explicit.
next_steps: Integration lane exact native.py patch: change `Native Kernel v21` to `Native Kernel v22`. After the sentence ending `decompositions over prime fields.`, insert: `Typed uint64 kernels support full-word &, |, ^, <<, and >>, plus augmented scalar/buffer forms. Left shift wraps modulo 2^64; right shift is logical. Counts are 0..63 (64+ raises OverflowError; negative counts fail uint64 validation). The native-bitwise marker preserves Sage-mode xor and gives dynamic Sage.js checked exact Number/BigInt behavior; CPython's annotation alias remains int.` Format every code/token name with Markdown backticks in the actual docstring.

Integration lane: rerun pnpm test:compiler and pnpm test:integration after rebasing onto the current integration base and preparing its native cache; investigate only if the recorded unrelated matrix/polynomial failures remain.
The test manifest follow-up is already complete in this lane: test/native-uint64-bitwise.cjs is registered in test/node-test-manifest.cjs.
